newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes still working with FAA.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes still working with FAA.

text.p: Great Lakes Aviation Ltd said Wednesday it continues to work with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration, but the airline will not rush to resume flights.

"We are making excellent progress inspecting our fleet, and we are hopeful of a return to service as soon as possible, but we are not rushing it," Doug Voss, Great Lakes president and chief executive, said in a statement.
The airline had said earlier it hoped to resume limited service on Thursday.

Spencer, Iowa-based Great Lakes voluntarily suspended all flights last Friday after the FAA told the carrier it faced a suspension of its operating authority due to flying "unairworthy aircraft". Great Lakes operates commuter flight for UAL Corp's United Airlines and for Midway Airlines.

Great Lakes said that by mid-Wednesday, the airline and the FAA had thoroughly inspected and approved four of its 53 aircraft. There were no safety discrepancies with any of the airplanes, the company said.
Voss said Great Lakes expects to resume service on a limited basis and gradually add flights and markets as the airline and the FAA complete the inspections.

"We'll resume service when the FAA, the airline and our employees have affirmed that we safely serve the public, as we always have," he said. "When Great Lakes resumes service after this rigorous inspection, the public can be confident that we will be operating to the highest levels of safety."
The company said service would likely begin on United Express routes from O'Hare Airport in Chicago, but did not specify when.
Great Lakes could not be reached for additional comment.
